answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make co-signing the costly act. Before a key accepts work at the shared task wharf, each distinct partner whose output it co-signs adds a bond: the k-th partner adds 50×k² POA, locked for a 60-epoch voyage. A key with 3 partners locks 700; a clone co-signing for 1,000 siblings locks about 16.7 billion, near twenty epochs of issuance. A fraud proof against any key spreads as a ripple, slashing every partner bond touching it. Weakness: farms that skip co-signing, which forfeits the attestation income clones exist to harvest.
